findings.message: When `normalized` is empty (e.g. input is `''`, or consists only of characters stripped by the separator/trim replaces such as `'---'` or `'!!!'`), `truncated` is `''` and `truncated[0]` is `undefined`. Calling `.toLowerCase()` on `undefined` throws a TypeError.
findings.consequence: slugify('') or slugify('---') now throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toLowerCase')` at runtime instead of returning '' as before this change, crashing any caller that previously relied on an empty-string result for non-alphanumeric input.
findings.recommendedAction: Guard the empty case before indexing, e.g. `return truncated.length === 0 ? truncated : truncated[0].toLowerCase() + truncated.slice(1);`, or reorder so the case transform only runs on a non-empty string.
